messages.content: Columbia Basin is finally off my desk, so switch me to the Santa Fe weekend. Looking at Friday May 30 out of the Bay Area, Sunday or Monday back depending on Maya's time off. Can you compare flying into Santa Fe with one stop versus Albuquerque nonstop and driving up? Also hotels near the Plaza or Railyard, walkable dinner, parking, quiet room.
Yes. Two adults, correct? Do you want me to keep SFO first and only use Oakland or San Jose if the schedule or price is clearly better? Also, rough hotel ceiling per night?
Two adults. SFO first. OAK or SJC only if it is an obvious win. Hotel target maybe 250 to 350 a night before tax. Not luxury, just well reviewed and not noisy.

I checked the Friday outbound with both return choices. The clean Albuquerque plan is SFO-ABQ nonstop, Friday 2:20 p.m.-5:55 p.m., about $304 per person; Monday return 1:45 p.m.-3:25 p.m., or Sunday 5:20 p.m.-7:00 p.m. The Santa Fe airport plan is one stop through Denver, Friday 1:05 p.m.-7:10 p.m., about $552 per person; return is also through Denver. Best fit on schedule and fare is Albuquerque plus a rental car. Santa Fe airport is easier on ground time, but not $450 to $500 easier for two people unless you really want to avoid the drive.
How late would we actually get to Santa Fe Friday with ABQ? I do not want the first night to be just airport logistics.

With checked bag and rental pickup, figure leaving ABQ around 6:35 to 6:50 and reaching a Plaza-area hotel around 7:45. The Santa Fe one-stop lands about 7:10 and gets you to the hotel around 7:35 to 7:45, so Friday night is basically a wash. The big difference is the return: ABQ means leaving Santa Fe about 2.5 to 3 hours before flight; SAF is a 20-minute airport run.
Good, ABQ sounds less painful than I expected. Show me hotel options. Plaza or Railyard. Quiet matters more than being on the exact Plaza.

Shortlist: Inn on the Alameda, 4.6 guest rating, Plaza/Canyon Road edge, about $319 refundable king, parking and breakfast included, good dinner walkability, quieter feel. Hotel Santa Fe in the Railyard, 4.4, around $279, free parking, on-site restaurant and easy Railyard dinners, 12 to 15 minute walk to Plaza. Drury Plaza, 4.5, very central and good value with breakfast, but busier and parking runs extra. Eldorado, 4.3, closest to Plaza action, nice but more hotel traffic and valet/parking fees.
Inn on the Alameda looks like the vibe. Do they have in-room coffee and a mini-fridge? Not a deal breaker for this one, but useful.

The refundable king listing shows a coffee maker, and the room notes say mini-fridge in king rooms, with availability confirmed by request. I would add a quiet-room note, away from elevator or ice machine, and ask them to confirm the mini-fridge before final booking.
Rental car: compact is fine? We may do Bandelier or just use it for the ABQ transfer.

Compact is fine for the ABQ-Santa Fe drive and Bandelier in normal weather. Current compact is about $186 Friday evening to Monday midday; compact SUV is about $234. If this is only airport transfer plus one day trip, compact is the best fit. If you want more margin for luggage and highway comfort, compact SUV is the acceptable backup.
Can you hold Monday as lead and Sunday as backup? Maya should know by Friday. What does Sunday save?

Sunday saves one hotel night and roughly $45 on the rental, with airfare nearly the same. It also compresses the trip: two nights, one full day, and a late Sunday flight. Monday gives you two full mornings and a less rushed checkout-to-airport rhythm. I would keep Monday if her time off clears.
Agreed. Do not book yet. Save ABQ as lead unless the Santa Fe airport option drops to within about 150 all-in for both of us. Inn on the Alameda first hotel.

Saved, not booked. Lead plan: Friday May 30 SFO-ABQ nonstop, compact rental car, Inn on the Alameda refundable king with quiet-room and mini-fridge confirmation request, Monday June 2 return after checkout. Acceptable backup: Sunday return if Monday PTO fails. Santa Fe airport stays a backup only if the total premium falls to about $150 or less for both travelers.

messages.content: Maya got Monday off. Let's finalize Santa Fe. Is the Inn on the Alameda refundable king still there, and is ABQ still enough cheaper than flying into Santa Fe?

Yes. Inn on the Alameda still has the refundable king at about $319 per night before tax, 4.6 guest rating, parking and breakfast included, and it accepts a quiet-room request. ABQ nonstop for two is $608 before seat or bag fees; SAF one-stop for two is $1,104. Even after the $186 compact rental, ABQ is still roughly $310 lower and the schedule is cleaner.
Good. Book the ABQ nonstop, Inn on the Alameda, and compact car. Standard economy, not basic. Add the quiet-room note. For seats, together matters more than window.

Confirming before purchase: two adults, Friday May 30 SFO-ABQ 2:20 p.m.-5:55 p.m.; Monday June 2 ABQ-SFO 1:45 p.m.-3:25 p.m.; compact car at ABQ Friday 6:30 p.m. to Monday 12:30 p.m.; Inn on the Alameda Friday through Monday checkout, refundable king. Seats available together are 18A/18B outbound and 20A/20B return, so you stay together and one seat is a window on each leg.
That works. Please book.
Booking now. The hotel cancellation cutoff is 48 hours before arrival; compact rental is pay-later with free cancellation; flights are standard economy with change credit rules, not basic. Continue?
Yes, issue it.

Booked. Flights: SFO-ABQ Friday 2:20 p.m. arriving 5:55 p.m.; ABQ-SFO Monday 1:45 p.m. arriving 3:25 p.m., confirmation SF8Q2L, seats 18A/18B and 20A/20B. Hotel: Inn on the Alameda, refundable king, confirmation IAL-7428, quiet room away from elevator and ice machine requested and mini-fridge noted for confirmation. Car: compact at ABQ, confirmation ABQ-6139, pickup 6:30 p.m. Friday and return 12:30 p.m. Monday.

messages.content: New work one. Nashville area distributor wants me for controls training on the brewery wastewater upgrade. Week of June 16. Monday travel, Tuesday 8 a.m. plant walk in Smyrna, Wednesday lunch-and-learn at their La Vergne branch. The demo case is supposed to hit their dock Monday afternoon, so I need enough time to rent a car, check the freight, and get to the hotel. Thursday morning sanitation audit is possible but not confirmed. Build the first pass flight, car, hotel. Do not book. For the hotel, compare branch versus plant, with ratings, parking, breakfast timing, dinner nearby, and room coffee/fridge if listed.
Got it. For the freight check, what is the latest useful arrival at the branch? And should I keep departure airport to SFO unless OAK or SJC is materially better?

Latest useful is 4:30 at the La Vergne dock. After that I can call someone, but I would rather see the case myself. SFO first; OAK/SJC only if they save a lot or avoid a bad connection. Hotel should be near either Smyrna plant or La Vergne branch, not downtown.

That 4:30 dock check makes the flight decision pretty tight. Monday options I would consider: United nonstop SFO-BNA 8:35 a.m.-2:52 p.m., about $438, rental by 3:35, La Vergne around 4:10 in normal traffic. United via Denver 10:45 a.m.-5:58 p.m., $392, one 72-minute layover, okay only if the distributor signs for freight without you. Later nonstop SFO-BNA 1:20 p.m.-7:36 p.m., comfortable departure but misses the freight check entirely. Best fit is the morning nonstop; acceptable backup is the Denver one-stop if freight is handled locally.
Can I avoid anything earlier than 8? I have prep the night before.

Yes. The 8:35 a.m. nonstop is the first option I would keep. There are earlier 6 a.m.-ish connections that arrive a little earlier, but they add a connection and do not buy enough value. The 8:35 protects the 4:30 dock check without turning the day into a dawn connection.
Good. Check OAK and SJC quickly, but I am not trying to save 80 dollars for a worse day.

OAK and SJC do not beat it. The OAK/Southwest routings connect and arrive after 5:30 p.m.; SJC options either connect through Denver or Phoenix or price higher than the SFO nonstop. I would leave Bay Area airport as SFO for this one.
Rental car: I may have to move a Pelican case and a small demo trainer if freight gets weird. Sedan seems risky.

Use a compact SUV. It is about $286 for Monday pickup to Thursday return, or about $218 if you come back Wednesday evening. A midsize sedan is $30 to $40 less but less flexible with the cases; a standard SUV is another $70 higher and seems unnecessary.
Now hotels. I want to compare staying by the branch versus by the plant. Parking, breakfast timing, nearby dinner, and whether coffee/fridge are listed.

Drive pattern favors Smyrna. From Smyrna hotels you are typically 8 to 12 minutes to the plant and 15 to 20 minutes to the La Vergne branch. Staying closer to the branch saves a few minutes Wednesday but makes Tuesday morning less comfortable and has thinner dinner options. Shortlist: Hampton Inn & Suites Nashville-Smyrna, 4.4 guest rating, $166, free parking, breakfast starts 6 a.m., coffee maker and mini-fridge listed, several dinner spots within a short drive. Hilton Garden Inn Nashville/Smyrna, 4.3, $178, free parking, on-site restaurant, breakfast from 6 a.m. for a charge, coffee/fridge listed. Home2 Suites Smyrna, 4.2, $159, free parking, bigger room with fridge/kitchenette, breakfast 6 a.m., limited dinner walkability. Hampton Inn La Vergne, 4.1, $151, close to branch, free parking/breakfast, coffee/fridge listed, but weaker dinner access and longer Tuesday drive.
Which one is the least annoying for Tuesday morning? I will be in safety boots and carrying the laptop bag.

Hampton Smyrna is the least annoying. It has the shortest simple drive to the Smyrna plant, breakfast starts early enough, and you are not relying on a hotel restaurant schedule. Hilton Garden is the backup if you want on-site dinner after the freight check. I would not put you in La Vergne unless Wednesday becomes the real center of gravity.
Make Hampton Smyrna lead. What about return flights with the Thursday uncertainty?

If there is no Thursday audit: Wednesday BNA-SFO nonstop at 5:25 p.m.-8:05 p.m. works after the lunch-and-learn if you can leave the branch by about 2:45. If the sanitation audit is added: Thursday BNA-SFO nonstop at 2:10 p.m.-4:50 p.m. works for an 8:00 to 10:30 audit; Thursday 5:25 p.m. is safer if the audit may run toward noon or if you need a debrief. I would avoid the 11 a.m. Thursday return.
Wednesday lunch-and-learn is noon to 2. Add cleanup and distributor talk, so leave branch 3 at earliest.

Then the Wednesday 5:25 p.m. nonstop still works but has little slack for Nashville traffic and rental return. A 6:45 p.m. one-stop through Denver adds a connection and gets you home late, but it gives more breathing room. If you are already unsure about Thursday, the cleaner move may be to plan for Thursday return and shorten only if the audit is cancelled early.
Hotel cancellation/change rules matter here. Can we book Monday through Thursday checkout and drop Wednesday night if audit dies?

Hampton's refundable rate allows cancellation or date changes until 6 p.m. local the day before arrival, but once you check in, dropping the last night depends on the front desk. Safer structure: book Monday and Tuesday as the core stay, and hold Wednesday night separately on a refundable reservation until the audit is confirmed. If you want less admin, book all three nights and accept that Wednesday night may not be removable after check-in.
Save the cleaner admin version for now: Monday through Thursday checkout, refundable, but no booking. I should know about the audit by Friday. Keep the 8:35 nonstop outbound and compact SUV.

Saved, not booked. Lead plan: Monday June 16 SFO-BNA nonstop 8:35 a.m.-2:52 p.m., compact SUV, freight check at La Vergne dock around 4:10 if traffic behaves, Hampton Inn & Suites Nashville-Smyrna Monday through Thursday checkout on a refundable rate. Return placeholder: Thursday 2:10 p.m. nonstop if the sanitation audit is 8:00-10:30; Thursday 5:25 p.m. if it may run late; Wednesday 5:25 p.m. only if the audit is cancelled and the branch wrap-up is done by 3. Open item: get the audit decision by Friday before we book.
